Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 7995 of 2023
Applicant :- Badal Chauhan

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Kshitij Tiwari

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Umesh Chandra Yadav Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
Heard Sri Kshitij Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Umesh Chandra Yadav, learned counsel for the informant and Dr. S.B. Maurya, learned AGA-I for the State.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
289 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366 IPC and Section 7/8 POCSO Act and 3(2)(v) SC/ST Act, Police Station Balua, District Chandauli during pendency of the trial.

FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and two others and according to the FIR applicant with the help of two others enticed away the minor daughter of the informant aged about 15 years.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and applicant neither abducted nor kidnapped nor enticed away the minor daughter of the informant and this fact is evident from the statement of victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.

He next submits that from the statement of victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. it appears that she herself called the applicant and thereafter both went to Delhi and applicant did not make any physical relationship with her.

He next submits that applicant could not Badal Chauhan vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35599723/
1 get the statement of victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. but from the bail rejection order, it appears that in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. she reiterated her earlier statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: , therefore, it appears that in both the statements victim did not make any accusation against the applicant.
He further submits that in the present matter applicant is in jail since 31.01.2023.

Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that victim is the minor girl aged about 15 years and applicant had gone with her but they could not dispute the fact that there is no allegation against the applicant either in the statement of victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. or 164 Cr.P.C. that he enticed away the victim.
Learned counsel for the informant further submits that applicant is also accused in a case relates to offence under Section 498A IPC, which was lodged against him and his family members.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

From the perusal of statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. it appears that victim did not make any accusation against the applicant and she had gone along with the applicant according to her own wish and when her statement under section 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded then also she stated the same facts.

Although, statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has not been appended in the instant bail application but in the bail rejection order court concerned observed that in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. victim stated that applicant did not entice her.
Further, in the present matter applicant is in jail since 31.01.2023.
From the discussion made above, in view of this Court, it is a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
In the light of discussions made above, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant - Badal Chauhan be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
